clue.text: Aggravate a legendary American sports commentator

definitions.meaning: to aggravate someone is to infuriate or anger them
John ..., the NFL coach turned famous American football broadcaster

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses hold: a verb for driving someone mad with irritation, and the surname of the celebrated football broadcaster John.

clue.text: Family member cuts salami in pieces — delicious!

indicators.note: the relative slices into the scrambled sausage, so it sits inside those letters
salami cut into pieces has its letters broken up and reassembled

parts.note: bro is informal for brother, a member of the family

explanation.surface: A relative slices up the salami, and the result tastes wonderful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in pieces' gives the scrambled AMSIAL; 'cuts' looks like the knife's work but means the relative goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambrosia was the food of the gods, so the adjective describes anything divinely tasty.

clue.text: Board game passes quickly

definitions.meaning: a pub game of throwing arrows at a dartboard
to dart is to move swiftly, so this is the third-person verb

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the pub game played on a board; the other is the verb for moving rapidly, as a bird flits past.

clue.text: Such inexperience, with government involvement, could be negative

indicators.note: says the word negative could be rearranged into the answer once another letter joins in

explanation.surface: Inexperience combined with official meddling might turn out badly.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: the answer plus G (government) can be rearranged as NEGATIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Naivety is innocence or lack of worldly experience, so the noun matches 'inexperience'.

clue.text: Gift arranged in advance around the start of November

indicators.note: the preset word wraps round the single letter

parts.note: preset means settled or arranged beforehand

indicators.note: the first letter of the word November is taken

explanation.surface: A present bought early, ahead of the holidays starting in November.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts N, from 'the start of November', inside PRESET.
explanation.definitionFit: A present is a gift handed to someone.

clue.text: Delivered shelled nuts, free from duty

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the remaining letters are jumbled
shelled means the outer casing is stripped, so the outside letters of Delivered go

explanation.surface: Someone delivered shelled nuts and was then let off work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shelled' strips Delivered to ELIVERE, and 'nuts' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To relieve a sentry or worker is to take over their post so they are off duty.

clue.text: Wise guy set college alarm off

indicators.note: off means out of order or wrong, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: college is abbreviated to C and alarm is kept as written, the two joining the shuffled pool

explanation.surface: A joker sets the college alarm ringing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' looks like the alarm being switched off, but it signals that the letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A smart alec is a know-all, someone who is irritatingly clever, exactly the sarcastic sense of 'wise guy'.

clue.text: First and foremost, nearly all sexists are lovers of Hooters

indicators.note: the foremost letters of each word in this run are taken

explanation.surface: A jab at the clientele of the Hooters restaurant chain, implying most are sexist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hooters' is slang for noses here, not the restaurant; 'of Hooters' therefore means relating to the nose.
explanation.definitionFit: Nasal is the adjective for the nose, and hooter is slang for nose.

clue.text: It's rarer to change — within the confines of TV — how the BBC traditionally broadcast

indicators.note: the scrambled letters sit inside the word for TV

parts.note: telly is British informal for television

indicators.note: changing the letters means rearranging them

explanation.surface: A grumble that rare things are changing inside television's old broadcasting world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to change' scrambles the letters to RRESTRIA. Before satellite and streaming, BBC television went out from ground-based transmitters.
explanation.definitionFit: Before satellite and online, the BBC transmitted over land-based aerial networks, which is terrestrial television.

clue.text: Thwarted upon taking it, run back

indicators.note: the word for upon takes in the other letters

parts.note: upon in the sense of over, above

indicators.note: back means the short sequence is read in reverse

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: Plans foiled once someone took it and ran back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses only 'it' plus the run, giving RTI; 'upon' must be read as 'over'.
explanation.definitionFit: An abortive attempt fails to achieve its aim, as if it had been frustrated or blocked.

clue.text: I have trouble going westbound to the London area to make a connection

indicators.note: in an across clue, westbound means right to left, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: to ail is to be unwell or in difficulty
SE is the postal district for south-east London

explanation.surface: A commuter struggling on a westbound train into London to make a connection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going westbound' reverses only the first part, giving LIAI, since across entries read west to east.
explanation.definitionFit: To liaise is to act as a link or cooperate between parties, a synonym for linking up.

clue.text: Make out on the way back? Excellent!

indicators.note: coming back means the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: to make out something is to spot or discern it

explanation.surface: A couple kissing on the journey home, and someone approves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make out' looks like kissing but means to see.
explanation.definitionFit: Tops is informal for the best, an exclamation of approval like 'brilliant'.

clue.text: Creepy-sounding place that's hard to get to

definitions.text: place that's hard to get to

indicators.note: the word for creepy is said aloud, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: eerie means creepy or spooky

explanation.surface: A spooky, remote spot that few can reach.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyrie is an eagle's nest built high on a crag, proverbially remote and inaccessible.

clue.text: After a short time, I will work

indicators.note: the contraction comes after the letter for time

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
contracted, I will becomes I'll

explanation.surface: Someone promising to get to work in a moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work' is the farming sense, not a job.
explanation.definitionFit: To till land is to work it by ploughing and preparing it for crops.

clue.text: Make holes in baked dish with pricker evenly

parts.note: a pie is a dish baked in an oven

indicators.note: the even-numbered letters of the word pricker are taken

explanation.surface: Instructions to prick a pie crust with a fork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'evenly' takes letters 2, 4 and 6 of pricker: RCE.
explanation.definitionFit: To pierce is to puncture or perforate something.

clue.text: Mr Fix It's good name in New York is bolstered by a flyer

indicators.note: in a down clue, being propped up means the second part sits beneath the first

parts.note: rep is American slang for reputation, one's good name
an airman is a pilot or aviator

explanation.surface: A handyman with a good New York reputation is helped by a pilot.
explanation.definitionFit: Mr Fix-It is a nickname for a handyman, someone who mends things.

clue.text: Run off with your old secret

parts.note: to run off with something is to steal it
thy is archaic for your

explanation.surface: Eloping with your former partner, kept quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealthy means furtive or done covertly, an adjective matching secret.

clue.text: It provides links for a website — one flashily advertising mobile communication

definitions.text: It provides links for a website

parts.note: a hyper is one who hypes, promoting something showily
a text is a message sent by mobile phone

explanation.surface: A web link offered by someone flashily promoting phone messaging.
explanation.definitionFit: Hypertext is the markup with clickable links joining web pages.

clue.text: Pest control ad leaflet is full of rubbish

indicators.note: the leaflet word is filled by the rubbish word

parts.note: a flyer is a promotional handbill
pap is worthless, trivial stuff

explanation.surface: A complaint that a pest-control advertising flyer is nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pest control' reads as part of the advert, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Flypaper is sticky paper hung up to trap insects, a form of pest control.

clue.text: Strip for very little money

definitions.meaning: a comic strip, here Charles Schulz's long-running one about Charlie Brown
a trivial sum, as in being paid a pittance

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the comic strip starring Snoopy; the other is slang for a tiny, paltry payment.

clue.text: A French shop that is wanting to reject instructions for prepping food

indicators.note: rejecting sends the letters back, so they are read in reverse
wanting means lacking, so these letters are dropped

parts.note: épicerie is French for a grocer's shop
ie is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A French grocer that has thrown out the cooking instructions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanting' removes IE from EPICERIE to leave EPICER, which 'to reject' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: A recipe sets out the steps and ingredients for making a dish.

clue.text: Americans not about to go barmy for The Ashes?

indicators.note: going barmy means going mad, so the letters are scrambled
not removes the letters for about from the word

parts.note: ca, from circa, means about

explanation.surface: Americans going crazy about the Ashes, England and Australia's cricket series.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' leaves AMERINS, which 'to go barmy' rearranges. The Ashes is the England–Australia Test cricket series, named after a burnt cricket bail.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashes left after cremation are a person's remains, the question mark flagging the cricket misdirection.

clue.text: Almost the final house

definitions.meaning: a ...-final is the round just before the final
a ...-detached house, sharing one wall with its neighbour

explanation.definitionFit: Short for semi-final, the stage one before the final, and for a semi-detached house, the classic British suburban home.

clue.text: Identical, bespoke-quality trousers

indicators.note: to trouser is to pocket, so the phrase takes the letters in

explanation.surface: Two pairs of identical, tailored trousers of fine quality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trousers' is a verb meaning pockets, signalling that the letters are held within.
explanation.definitionFit: Equal means the same in amount or value, close to identical.

clue.text: A large weapon creates fear

parts.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
an arm is a weapon, as in firearms

explanation.surface: A big gun causes terror.
explanation.definitionFit: Alarm is sudden fright or anxiety at danger.

clue.text: Murdoch is upset to get an intelligent personal assistant

indicators.note: upset means overturned, so the name is read backwards

parts.note: Iris Murdoch, the British novelist and philosopher

explanation.surface: A media mogul named Murdoch is annoyed at acquiring a clever aide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Murdoch' suggests Rupert, the media tycoon, but it is the novelist Iris.
explanation.definitionFit: Apple's voice-controlled software helper on iPhones is a virtual assistant.

clue.text: Strain is mounting and getting on top of the First Lady

indicators.note: in a down clue, sitting on top puts this piece first
in a down clue, mounting means going upward, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: Eve was the first woman in the Bible

explanation.surface: Pressure is rising and overwhelming the president's wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The First Lady' suggests a president's wife, but it is the biblical Eve.
explanation.definitionFit: To sieve is to strain, passing something through a mesh, as a verb.

clue.text: Two sets of male uniforms provide clothing for Pacific islanders

indicators.note: the group of letters appears twice in a row

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for uniform, so two of them

explanation.surface: Two batches of men's uniforms are supplied to Pacific islanders.
explanation.definitionFit: A muumuu is a loose, brightly patterned dress from Hawaii.

clue.text: Look horribly tired, having at first expectantly waited around

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look

indicators.note: horribly signals the letters are badly mangled
the first letter of expectantly is taken

explanation.surface: Someone looks exhausted after waiting around in hope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horribly' rearranges TIRED plus E, the first letter of 'expectantly', to give ITERED.
explanation.definitionFit: To loiter is to hang about idly, and the past tense matches 'waited around'.

clue.text: American politician conclusively sells out an entire state

indicators.note: out means disordered, so the letters are jumbled
the concluding letter of politician is taken

explanation.surface: A US politician ultimately sells out an entire state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges N, the last of 'politician', with SELLS to make LLNESS. 'State' is a condition, not a US state.
explanation.definitionFit: Allness is the quality of being total or complete, a state of wholeness.

clue.text: Some Aussies taking an afternoon nap

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some Australians having an afternoon snooze.
explanation.definitionFit: A siesta is a rest taken after lunch in hot countries.
